title: Get or renew a local business license (BPOL)
question: I am starting or running a business in Albemarle County. How do I get a business license, and when must I renew it?
office: Department of Finance & Budget, Office of Revenue Administration (Business & Personal Tax Unit); the Director of Finance holds the commissioner of the revenue's assessing powers under the county executive form of government
summary: Albemarle County requires a business license for each business and each place of business in the county, including one run from home. The county has no Commissioner of the Revenue: the Department of Finance & Budget's Office of Revenue Administration issues licenses. A new business gets zoning approval, then emails, mails or faxes the New Business License Application; it cannot open an account online. The county's forms allow 30 days from the start date, but state law and the County Code say to apply before starting. Every license is renewed by March 1, online or on paper, using last year's gross receipts. Up to $25,000: no fee, but file. Over $25,000 and under $100,000: $50. $100,000 or more: a rate by business category, billed in May and due June 15. Late filing costs 10%.

steps.step: Check whether your business needs a county license, and how many
steps.how: You need an Albemarle County business license if your business has a definite place of business in the county (an office or location used for business for 30 consecutive days or more). If you have no business location anywhere and live in the county, your home counts, so home-based businesses are covered. You need a separate license for each business category and each location, even at the same address. Peddlers, itinerant merchants, carnivals, amusement-machine operators and out-of-county contractors doing more than $25,000 of work in the county also need one. State law and County Code § 8-200(C) let you choose instead to hold one license for several businesses at one location, if each is licensable there, they are taxed at the same rate (or you agree to pay the highest rate on all of them), and you give the Director of Finance the information asked for about them. The county's pages do not mention this option. State law exempts some activities, for example the receipts of 501(c)(3) charities (except unrelated business income) and farm products sold by the person who grew them.

steps.step: Get zoning approval from the Community Development Department
steps.who: Business owner, applying to the Community Development Department
steps.how: Apply in the county's Civic Access portal. A business in commercial or industrial space needs a Zoning Clearance; there are also separate clearances for a family day home, a mobile food vendor, sales or events at an agricultural operation, and agritourism, events or amplified music at a farm winery, brewery or distillery. Growing and harvesting farm products, and producing, selling or tasting wine, beer or spirits, need no clearance. A business run from the home you live in needs a Home Occupation Clearance, approved before you start: Minor or Major in the Rural Area, Class A in a residential district. A Class B home occupation in a residential district needs a special use permit instead. The clearance confirms the use is allowed at your location and notes parking and other limits. It may also need approval from the Architectural Review Board, a Certified Engineer's Report, or Health Department or VDOT approval. The license application lists zoning approval as required, but says it does not have to be obtained before you apply for the license.
steps.deadline: A Home Occupation Clearance must be approved before the business starts; the pages read give no deadline for other clearances
steps.fee: Probably $60 for a zoning clearance (the fee schedule's "All other uses" line); $30 for a home occupation clearance; $1,185 for a Class B home occupation special use permit; each plus a 4% technology surcharge (see fees)

steps.step: Register a trade name or business entity with the SCC, and get any state trade license
steps.who: Business owner; State Corporation Commission (Clerk's Office); for contractors, the state Board for Contractors
steps.how: If you will do business under any name other than your own legal name, file a certificate of assumed or fictitious name with the State Corporation Commission. The county may not issue the license until you show it evidence of that filing. A corporation, LLC, partnership or business trust should have its SCC registration ready. A contractor needs a state contractor's license, or a sworn statement that it is not required to hold one. It must also certify that it has workers' compensation coverage where the law requires it.
steps.deadline: Before applying for the county license

steps.step: Fill in the New Business License Application
steps.how: Use the county's 2026 New Business License Application (form dated 11/2025). Enter the date the business began in the county, the type of business, the legal and trade names, and your Social Security number or federal EIN. If you have an EIN, the county may not insist on your SSN. Add the addresses and contact details. Describe the business and pick its category. With no full prior year, enter your estimated gross receipts from the start date to December 31; if you began during 2025, give 2025 actual receipts and a 2026 estimate. The tax is computed on the estimate and corrected later. Add any ABC (alcohol) licenses and other activities, list vehicles used more than 50% for business, and sign. Contractors attach their state contractor's license, a certificate of liability insurance, a schedule of gross receipts from all sources and a list of licenses bought in other localities.
steps.deadline: Within 30 days of the date the business began in Albemarle County, to avoid the 10% late filing penalty (state law and County Code § 8-201(A) say before beginning business)

steps.step: Submit the application, documents and any fee due to the Office of Revenue Administration
steps.who: Business owner, filing with the Office of Revenue Administration (Business & Personal Tax Unit)
steps.how: A new business cannot open an account in the online portal. Email the signed application and documents to tax@albemarle.org. Or mail them to County of Albemarle, 401 McIntire Rd, Room 133, Charlottesville, VA 22902 (the form says Suite 133), or fax them to 434-243-7906. The county's pages and form do not mention filing a new application in person. Call 434-296-5852 to have an application mailed, or book a virtual or in-person appointment with a tax specialist. Pay any $50 license fee or flat tax with the application, by check payable to Albemarle County. An incomplete application or missing documents may lead to denial and late penalties.
steps.deadline: Within 30 days of beginning business (county practice); before beginning business under state law and County Code § 8-201(A)
steps.fee: $0 if gross receipts are $25,000 or less; $50 if over $25,000 and under $100,000; a flat tax for listed activities; a rate-based tax if $100,000 or more (see fees)

steps.step: The county reviews the application and issues the license
steps.who: Director of Finance (who holds a commissioner of the revenue's powers), through the Office of Revenue Administration
steps.how: The office checks the documents and the classification. It will not issue a license until any delinquent county business license, real estate, personal property, meals, transient occupancy, severance and admissions taxes owed by the business are paid. For a trade name it needs evidence of the SCC filing. For a contractor it needs the state license number or proof of exemption, and the workers' compensation certification. Keep the license receipt at the business, and show it when an authorized county officer asks.
steps.quote: satisfactory evidence that all delinquent business license, real estate, personal property, meals, transient occupancy, severance, and admissions taxes owed by the business to the County

steps.step: If gross receipts are $100,000 or more, pay the license tax by June 15
steps.who: Business owner, paying the Department of Finance & Budget
steps.how: At $100,000 or more in gross receipts you pay a tax at your category's rate instead of the $50 fee. Examples: $0.20 per $100 for retail, $0.36 per $100 for repair, personal, business and other services, $0.58 per $100 for financial, real estate and professional services, and $0.16 per $100 for contractors. The county mails BPOL tax bills in May. You can pay in the Business Tax portal (e-check is free; cards cost 2.50% for credit or 2.35% for debit, minimum $1.95). You can also pay by mail as the bill instructs, at the 24/7 kiosk, in person at 401 McIntire Road, or in a drop box (no cash). The new business form says the tax is due when you apply, and that a business applying after mid-June has 30 days to pay (see caveats).
steps.deadline: June 15 of the license year (June 15, 2026 on the 2026 renewal form)
steps.fee: Gross receipts times the category rate (see fees)

steps.step: For the first three years, renew on the full application
steps.how: For its first three years, a new business renews on the full New Business License Application, not the short renewal form, and replaces its estimate with actual receipts. After the base year the county adjusts the estimated tax to the actual amount. If you overestimated, you get a credit against the next year's tax.

steps.step: Renew every license every year by March 1
steps.who: Every licensed business, filing with the Office of Revenue Administration
steps.how: File a renewal for each license and each county location, reporting the previous calendar year's actual gross receipts. ABC sales count in retail or wholesale receipts. The county mails a BPOL renewal notice that holds the details you need. File online in the Albemarle County Business Tax Online Filing and Payment Portal (you need your county account number), on the county's digital renewal form, or on the downloadable PDF. Send the PDF by email, mail or fax, drop it off at the McIntire Road office building during business hours, or leave it in one of the "Payment" boxes in the McIntire Road parking lot. Contractors must include a copy of their workers' compensation verification. From 2026, homestay and other accommodations providers must also file an annual attestation with the renewal. A new line of business or a new location needs a new application.
steps.deadline: March 1 each year (the 2026 renewal form gives March 2, 2026, because March 1 fell on a Sunday)
steps.fee: $50 or a flat tax due with the renewal by March 1; a rate-based tax is billed in May and due June 15

steps.step: File the renewal even if gross receipts were $25,000 or less
steps.how: At $25,000 or less in gross receipts there is no fee, and the County Code waives the license requirement. The county still tells you to file every year: its renewal page says you need to file, and its deadlines page says you must still file by March 1, while its FAQ says you are advised to file, to record your receipts and exemption and so that it can remind you if you go over the threshold. Do not send a payment.

steps.step: If you cannot file on time, ask for an extension before the due date
steps.who: Business owner, asking the Director of Finance
steps.how: The Director of Finance may extend the time to file for reasonable cause. The extension may depend on paying a reasonable estimate of the tax on time. Interest runs from the due date on any balance, and if the estimate turns out to be unreasonable, a 10% penalty applies to the part paid late. The county's pages do not say how to ask, so contact the office before the due date.
steps.deadline: Not fixed by law or on the county's pages; ask before the filing due date (March 1 for a renewal; for a new business, before it begins, or at the latest within the 30 days the county's forms allow)
steps.quote: The Director of Finance may grant an extension of time in which to file an application for a license, for reasonable cause.
steps.source: Albemarle County Code § 8-201(C) (Ordinance No. 19-8(1); the same words are in proposed Ordinance No. 22-8( ) & 22-15( ))

steps.step: Late filing or late payment: penalties, interest and abatement
steps.how: The county's forms state a 10% penalty for filing late (County Code § 8-201(D) says the Director of Finance may impose it). If a $50 fee or flat tax is not paid by the March due date, a 10% late payment penalty applies, plus interest at 10% a year from April 1. If a rate-based tax is not paid by June 15, the 10% penalty applies from June 16, plus interest from July 1 (2026 dates). When both the filing and the payment are late, only the late filing penalty is charged, unless you have a history of noncompliance. A penalty is waived or removed if the lateness was not your fault: you must show you acted responsibly and that events beyond your control caused it.
steps.fee: 10% of the tax; interest at 10% a year

steps.step: Tell the county when the business closes, moves out or changes address
steps.who: Business owner, notifying the Business & Personal Tax Unit
steps.how: If the business has closed or moved out of the county, tick the closure box on the renewal and give the closure date, or tell the Business & Personal Tax Unit by email or letter. Report a new mailing or location address on page 2 of the renewal. If your tax is based on gross receipts and you close during the license year, the County Code may entitle you to a refund (§ 8-603, conditions apply). Business tangible personal property is a separate tax with its own rules.

steps.step: If you disagree with an assessment or your business classification, file a written appeal
steps.who: Business owner or authorized representative, writing to the Department of Finance & Budget, Revenue Administration - Assessments Unit
steps.how: Send a written administrative appeal, filed in good faith. Include the taxpayer's name and address, federal tax identification number and county account number(s). If someone else files, add a power of attorney or letter of representation. Attach a copy of the assessment, a detailed explanation of your position and the relief you want. The office may hold a conference if you ask, ask for more documents, or audit. While a timely and complete appeal is pending, collection of the disputed amount stops, unless the county finds that collection would be jeopardized by delay, that you have not answered a request for information within a reasonable time, or that the appeal is frivolous. Interest still accrues, but no further penalty is added. See escalation for the next steps.
steps.deadline: Within one year from the last day of the tax year assessed, or one year from the appealable event, whichever is later; a classification appeal can be filed at any time

escalation.trigger: Assessment increased, refund denied, tax assessed where none was before, estimated assessment when no application was filed, or classification disputed (an appealable event)
escalation.next: Director of Finance (Department of Finance & Budget, Revenue Administration - Assessments Unit), by written administrative appeal
escalation.deadline: Within one year from the last day of the tax year assessed, or within one year from the appealable event, whichever is later; a classification appeal at any time
escalation.quote: may file an administrative appeal of the assessment within one year from the last day of the tax year for which such assessment is made, or within one year from the date of the appealable event, whichever is later, with the commissioner of the revenue or other local assessing official.

escalation.trigger: A timely and complete administrative appeal is pending
escalation.next: Collection of the disputed amount is suspended until the Director's final determination, unless collection would be jeopardized by delay, the taxpayer has not answered a request for information within a reasonable time, or the appeal is found frivolous (interest still accrues, no further penalty)
escalation.quote: collection activity with respect to the amount in dispute relating to any assessment by the commissioner of the revenue or other assessing official shall be suspended until a final determination is issued by the commissioner of the revenue or other assessing official

escalation.trigger: No final determination after the appeal has been pending more than one year
escalation.next: Tax Commissioner (Virginia Department of Taxation), after at least 30 days' written notice to the Director of Finance
escalation.deadline: After more than one year without a decision, on at least 30 days' written notice
escalation.quote: elect to treat the appeal as denied and appeal the assessment or classification of the taxpayer's business to the Tax Commissioner in accordance with the provisions of subdivision 6

escalation.trigger: Director of Finance's determination is adverse
escalation.next: Tax Commissioner (Virginia Department of Taxation); serve a copy of the appeal on the Director of Finance
escalation.deadline: Within 90 days of the date of the Director's determination; the Tax Commissioner decides within 90 days of receipt unless both sides are told it will take longer
escalation.quote: may appeal such assessment or determination to the Tax Commissioner within 90 days of the date of the determination by the commissioner of the revenue or other assessing official.

escalation.trigger: Notice of intent to appeal to the Tax Commissioner given
escalation.next: Collection of the disputed amount is suspended until the Tax Commissioner's final determination, if the appeal is filed and served within 30 days of the notice
escalation.deadline: Appeal filed and served within 30 days of the notice of intent
escalation.quote: collection activity with respect to the amount in dispute relating to any assessment by the commissioner of the revenue or other assessing official shall be suspended until a final determination is issued by the Tax Commissioner

escalation.trigger: Still aggrieved after the Tax Commissioner's determination, or choosing to go straight to court
escalation.next: Circuit Court of Albemarle County ("Albemarle County" is the named party)
escalation.deadline: Whichever is latest: three years from the last day of the tax year, one year from the assessment, one year from the Tax Commissioner's final determination, or one year from a final determination under § 58.1-3981
escalation.quote: apply for relief to the circuit court of the county or city wherein such assessment was made.

escalation.trigger: Late filing or late payment penalty charged although the lateness was not the taxpayer's fault
escalation.next: Director of Finance (ask for the penalty to be abated; show you acted responsibly and that events beyond your control caused the lateness)
escalation.quote: If the failure to file or pay was not the fault of the taxpayer, the penalties shall not be imposed, or if imposed, shall be abated by the official who assessed them.

escalation.trigger: Unsure how the license tax or a classification applies to your business
escalation.next: Director of Finance (written ruling; give all relevant facts)
escalation.quote: Any taxpayer or authorized representative of a taxpayer may request a written ruling regarding the application of a local license tax to a specific situation from the commissioner of the revenue or other assessing official.

escalation.trigger: Business licensed in several localities and their methods would tax more than 100% of its gross receipts, with no apportionment agreement
escalation.next: Department of Taxation (advisory opinion; give notice to the Director of Finance). First tell the Director of Finance; the Director must make a good-faith effort to reach an apportionment agreement with the other localities, and either side may ask for the opinion if none is reached
escalation.quote: either the assessor or taxpayer may seek an advisory opinion from the Department of Taxation pursuant to § 58.1-3701

caveats: Albemarle County's website (www.albemarle.org) refuses automated readers, so the county pages and PDFs cited here are Internet Archive copies: they show the pages as they were when copied. That includes the three forms. The live pages may have changed since; confirm on them before you act. The 2027 forms will carry new dates. The County's Terms and Conditions bar reposting its content without written permission, so the County's own words are not reprinted on this page; each step links the County page instead.

Local law. The County Code is published on Municode, whose terms forbid automated access, so the current Code text has not been checked. The County Code quotes come from ordinance documents in the county's Legistar system (webapi.legistar.com). Sections 8-103 to 8-702, and § 8-201(A), (B), (C) and (D)(2), are quoted from the proposed final text of Ordinance No. 19-8(1). The county's 2022 documents cite that ordinance as adopted on April 17, 2019, but the draft is a redline, so the quotes give the adopted reading: underlined and unmarked text kept, struck text dropped. § 8-201(D)(1) and the renumbered Division 7 rate sections are quoted from the 2022 proposed ordinances (Legistar matters 22-450 and 22-481, both heard on November 2, 2022). Legistar records no action on either, so their adoption is not confirmed. The rates are the same in the 2019 text, so only the section numbers (and "ten" for "10" percent in § 8-201(D)(1)) depend on it. A Legistar title search for matters since December 2022 found no later Chapter 8 amendment.

New business deadline. The county's FAQ and application say to apply within 30 days of beginning business to avoid the 10% late filing penalty. State law (§ 58.1-3703.1(A)(2)(a)) and County Code § 8-201(A) say to apply before beginning business. The safe course is to apply before opening.

When a new business pays a rate-based tax is unclear. The new business application says a rate-based tax is due when you apply. It also says bills go out in mid-May 2026, gives a June 16, 2026 cutoff (the renewal form and County Code § 8-201(B) say June 15), and says a business applying after June 16 has 30 days. Ask the office which date applies to you. The application also labels its 30-day rule both ways: Step 2 says apply within 30 days "TO AVOID 10% LATE FILING PENALTY", while its penalty section says a late new business application is charged a late-payment penalty of 10%, plus interest fees of 10% per annum."

Renewal date. County pages say March 1. The 2026 renewal form gives March 2, 2026, because March 1, 2026 was a Sunday. State law fixes March 1 unless the locality adopts a later date, no later than May 1. Albemarle's Code keeps March 1.

The $25,000 floor. County Code § 8-200(D), as enacted in 2019, waives the license requirement at gross receipts of $25,000 or less, yet the county asks those businesses to file every year anyway. State law would let a locality of this size waive licenses up to $200,000 (§ 58.1-3703.1(A)(1)). The county's wording of the bands also varies: the rate table says "less than $25,000" and "$100,000 and Over", the deadlines page says "greater than $100,000", and the forms and the renewal page say "$25,000 or less" and "$100,000 or more". The fees here follow the forms and the County Code.

Rate table. The county's BPOL rate table is headed "TAX PER $100,000 GROSS RECEIPTS", but its figures ($0.0020 for retail, for example) are rates per dollar, equal to the Code's $0.20 per $100. The table also lists a 0.50% utility rate, flat taxes (bondsmen $150, show and sale $50 to $600, fortunetellers $500, carnivals $500 or $25 a day, amusement machines $100 or $200, savings institutions $50) and local ABC license fees ($25 to $1,000). These are not all repeated in fees.
Population. The $50 fee cap and the $100,000 tax threshold apply because Albemarle has more than 50,000 people (2020 Census), per §§ 58.1-3703(A) and 58.1-3706(A).

Penalty waivers. The county's late penalty policy, on the Important Dates and Deadlines page, says penalties are not waived when a taxpayer relied on erroneous information from county staff. For the license tax, though, § 58.1-3703.1(A)(2)(d) and County Code § 8-201(D)(2)(b) count reasonable good-faith reliance on erroneous written information from the assessing official as an event beyond the taxpayer's control. Oral advice does not qualify. The policy also cites the general penalty sections (County Code § 15-103, Va. Code § 58.1-3916, which allow 10% or $10). The license forms state a 10% license penalty.

Appeal notice versus law. The county's Notice of Taxpayer Appeal Rights says that going straight to circuit court suspends collection on written notice. But § 58.1-3703.1(A)(7)(b)(5) and County Code § 8-206 say the suspension does not apply to a direct § 58.1-3984 filing made without first using the local and Tax Commissioner appeals. The notice also lists a Finance mailbox and a fax number that differ from the business tax unit's; they were not recorded.

Refusal of a license. No statute was found that gives a specific appeal from a refusal to issue a business license (for example because of delinquent local taxes, a missing SCC filing, or missing contractor documents). The administrative appeal covers assessments, refunds and classification. The practical route is to cure the defect. Court remedies against a refusal are not covered here. Operating without a license is a Class 2 misdemeanor under County Code § 8-103(A) (2019 text), and does not relieve the tax (§ 58.1-3700(B)).

No deadline for the local decision. State law sets no time limit for the Director of Finance to decide a license tax appeal. The only remedy for delay is the one-year rule in § 58.1-3703.1(A)(5)(e). The 90-day limit in § 58.1-3983.1 covers other local business taxes, not the license tax.

Tax Commissioner appeal form. Virginia Tax's page sends state-tax appeals to its Appeals Form. For local license tax appeals it says only that the appeal must contain what § 58.1-1821 requires, and that a copy must go to the local assessing officer. Whether to use the form is not stated, so it is not listed in forms. Advisory opinion requests use Form Rulings-Fee and may carry a fee.

Payments. The payment options page gives card fees of 2.50% (credit) and 2.35% (debit) for online payments, but swaps the two in its phone section, and lists the phone line (866-820-5450) only for real estate and personal property taxes. The P.O. Box 7604, Merrifield address is for check payments of bills. Applications and renewals go to 401 McIntire Road. The renewal form says renewals can go in the payment drop boxes in the McIntire Road parking lot. The payment options page says a drop box is open only from June 1 to 25 and from November 1 to December 5; it is not clear whether that limit covers the McIntire Road boxes or only the 5th Street one.

Separate processes not modelled here: the zoning clearance and home occupation clearance themselves (their requirements, review and the Class B special use permit process), SCC assumed-name filing, the state contractor's license, local ABC licenses, the homestay accommodations provider attestation (required with 2026 renewals), business tangible personal property returns (due May 1), and food and beverage, transient occupancy and short-term rental taxes.
Not described here: the online Business Tax portal (albemarlecountytaxes.org), the Microsoft Forms digital renewal, the Civic Access zoning portal and the appointment booking page.

One license for several businesses. The county's page says a separate license is needed for each business category, even at the same location. State law (§ 58.1-3703.1(A)(1)) and County Code § 8-200(C) let a person with several businesses at one place of business elect a single license if each business is licensable there, all are taxed at the same rate or the licensee accepts the highest rate, and the licensee supplies the information the Director asks for. Ask the office how to make the election.

Zoning fees. The Community Development fee schedule (Internet Archive copy of 2026-08-20) lists a $30 home occupation clearance, a $60 clearance for "All other uses", a $120 homestay clearance and a $1,185 special use permit for a Class B home occupation, plus a 4% technology surcharge. It does not name the business-in-commercial-space clearance, so the $60 line is the closest match, not a confirmed fee for it.

Site terms. The albemarle.org Terms and Conditions allow browsing for informational purposes but say no one may reuse or repost the site's content without written permission, so the County's own words are not reprinted on this page; each entry links the County page instead.

Privacy. Staff names and personal mailboxes on the zoning and home occupation pages, in the Legistar documents and on the court page were not recorded. Only office addresses, main lines, the tax@albemarle.org and cddinquiry@albemarle.org office mailboxes and official portals are listed. The Community Development line 434-296-5832 is the department's main number (the County Code page gives it for the department). The appointment link, as the county publishes it, contains the Assessments Unit's booking mailbox, which is an office mailbox.

corrections: legal_basis Va. Code § 58.1-3706(A): the quote started mid-sentence, after the words that make it a prohibition, so it read as the opposite of the statute (no license tax below $100,000 here). Replaced with the statute's next sentence (a business over $100,000 may be taxed at up to the listed rates); role changed to fee.

s1: added the single-license election for several businesses at one place of business (Va. Code § 58.1-3703.1(A)(1); County Code § 8-200(C)), with a state and a local legal_basis quote, and a caveat that the county's page does not mention it.

s2: the Home Occupations page says a Home Occupation Clearance must be approved before the business starts, and a Class B home occupation in a residential district needs a special use permit; the clearance types now match the zoning page (including that farm production and wine, beer or spirits production, sales and tastings need no clearance). Filled the deadline and fee, added form f6 (Home Occupations application) and four fees from the Community Development fee schedule.

County Code § 8-201(A), (B), (C) and (D)(2), and s11: the same words are in the 2019 text of Ordinance No. 19-8(1), whose adoption on April 17, 2019 the county's 2022 documents record, so these now cite that text; they no longer depend on the unconfirmed 2022 adoption. § 8-201(D)(1) stays on the 2022 text and notes the 2019 wording ("10 percent").
s9: added the in-person drop-off at the McIntire Road office building during business hours, which the 2026 renewal form lists.
s10: the county's renewal and deadlines pages say a business at $25,000 or less needs to (must) file; only the FAQ says it is advised to. The step had said the county only asks; reworded.
s11 deadline: neither the law nor the county's pages fix a time for asking for an extension, and a new business's legal due date is before it begins, not 30 days after; reworded.
s12: the County Code says the Director of Finance may impose the 10% penalty; the step now says the forms state it, not that it is automatic.

s14 and escalation rung 2: suspension of collection during a local appeal has three exceptions (jeopardy, no response to a request for information, frivolous appeal) under § 58.1-3703.1(A)(5)(d) and County Code § 8-204(E); added, with no further penalty while suspended.

Escalation rung 9: the taxpayer first notifies the Director of Finance, who must try in good faith to reach an apportionment agreement; either side may then seek the advisory opinion (§ 58.1-3703.1(A)(3)(c)).
Summary: no longer presents the 30-day window as the rule; it notes that state law and the County Code say to apply before starting.
Fees for the retail, direct retail, other-business, wholesale and rental rates: basis now notes the same rates are in the 2019 enacted text, so the amounts do not depend on the 2022 renumbering.

Caveats: rewrote the local-law caveat (verifier's judgement on the Legistar Web API, Legistar matter 22-481 for the Division 7 renumbering, no action recorded for either 2022 matter, no later Chapter 8 matter found); added the new business form's two labels for the 30-day penalty, the single-license option, the zoning fee mapping, the albemarle.org terms of use, and the department main line in the privacy caveat; updated the separate-processes caveat now that the home occupation page was read.
Sources: added the Home Occupations page, the Community Development Fees page, the albemarle.org Terms and Conditions (Internet Archive copies) and Legistar matter 22-481.
open_issues: www.albemarle.org still returns HTTP 403 to this client (robots.txt included, 2026-10-11). All 22 county-page and county-form quotes were confirmed word for word against Internet Archive copies (March to August 2026); the Internet Archive index shows the 2026-08-13/14 captures are the newest for the business license pages. Re-check the live pages, and the 2027 forms when they appear.

The current County Code text (Municode) was not read because of that site's terms. Adoption of the November 2, 2022 ordinances (Legistar matters 22-450 and 22-481) is not recorded in the Legistar Web API; this affects only the Division 7 section numbers and "ten" versus "10" percent in § 8-201(D)(1), not any amount or step.

Policy judgement for the user: the 18 County Code quotes in legal_basis, the s6 and s11 quotes and 8 fee quotes come from Legistar attachments read through the Legistar Web API (no robots.txt; published by Granicus for programmatic reads of public items) rather than albemarle.legistar1.com, whose robots.txt disallows crawlers. The verifier judged this acceptable. If the user disagrees, those quotes should come out.

County practice and law differ on the new-business deadline (30 days versus before beginning business) and the new-business payment date for a rate-based tax (due on application, June 15 or June 16, or 30 days after a late application). The steps state both; ask the office which applies.
The fee schedule does not name the business-in-commercial-space zoning clearance; the $60 "All other uses" fee is the closest match, not a confirmed fee for it.
No statute or county page was found giving a specific appeal from a refusal to issue a license; judicial remedies were not researched.
The albemarle.org terms of use bar reusing or reposting site content without written permission; whether publishing short quoted passages needs permission is for the user to decide.
Not opened or submitted: the Business Tax portal, the Microsoft Forms digital renewal, the Civic Access zoning portal and the booking page; what they ask for is unknown.
